F1.Stream Processor: computes the 5-minute windowed avg tip per mile per neighbourhood from the trip+fare join
F1.Gold Marts: owns the tips-per-mile-by-neighbourhood aggregate (§6) that the Semantic Model reads; stream writes silver, so gold is the handoff
F1.Semantic Model: avg tip per mile measure + neighbourhood relationship
F1.Dashboards: live neighbourhood map visual on the ops report

F2.Silver Transforms: conformed driver table from dispatch CDC joined to trips
F2.Gold Marts: driver scorecard model (trips, revenue, rating per driver per day)
F2.Semantic Model: per-driver measures incl. rating over the scorecard table

F3.Bronze Loader: land a brand-new event type into its bronze table
F3.Silver Transforms: conformed trip table must carry cancelled status / cancellation rows

F4.Stream Processor: new 15-minute ride count per zone window (currently 5-minute averages)
F4.Gold Marts: gold table over the new window so the Semantic Model (over gold) can read it
F4.Dashboards: Metric Alerts evaluates rules on dashboard visuals (§6), so the visual must exist

F5.Serving SQL Endpoint: hosts the deletion-request table the officer writes to (new store-specific table)
F5.Privacy Erasure Job: delete from bronze, propagate silver/gold, purge history, set status
F5.DAG Scheduler: new DAG to run the erasure job; Orchestrator owns scheduling

F6.Backfill Runner: finance-triggered parameterised DAG deletes partitions and reloads silver and gold; silver/gold rerun unchanged (§10)

keyChanges: F1: added Gold Marts. Both sets argued it and §6 agrees: Gold Marts' Responsibility names the tips-per-mile-by-neighbourhood aggregate and the Semantic Model is defined over gold tables, so the stream's silver window needs a gold model to reach Power BI.
F4: added Gold Marts for the same reason; applied consistently with F1 (Semantic Model reads gold, Stream Processor writes silver).
borderlineRule: Items listed under `borderline` are defensible but not required; they count as neither missing nor wrong.

X.F2 Bronze Loader: why restates its existing append behaviour; dispatch CDC already lands in bronze, no change named
X.F6 Gold Marts: daily revenue model simply reruns under the backfill (§10: silver and gold rebuilt from bronze); no model change
X.F6 Dashboards: revenue report reads the rebuilt gold via Direct Lake; nothing on the report changes

Y.F1 Event Ingest Hub: trip and fare hubs already exist and already partition by taxi id; feature uses them, does not change them
Y.F1 Pipeline Monitoring: shared platform service; feature asks for no new SLA or alert on the pipeline
Y.F2 Bronze Loader: same as X: existing append, no change
Y.F2 Pipeline Monitoring: shared service used not changed; failure alerting already exists for nightly runs
Y.F3 Dead-Letter Handler: generic per-source quarantine already covers a new event type; nothing to build
Y.F4 Pipeline Monitoring: feature's alert is the KPI alert (Metric Alerts); pipeline lag alerting is speculative scope

patterns: Y links Pipeline Monitoring on F1, F2 and F4 for SLA/lag alerting the feature never asked for; a shared platform service that is used, not changed.
Both sets link components that merely rerun or pass data through unchanged: Bronze Loader on F2 (both), Gold Marts on F6 (both), Dashboards on F6 (X only).
Y links the existing ingest edge and generic error path as if a new feature altered them: Event Ingest Hub on F1, Dead-Letter Handler on F3.

Y's whys tend to paraphrase the §6 Responsibility instead of naming the change (F2 Bronze Loader, F6 Silver Transforms); X's whys more often name the delta (F3 accepted_values test breaks, F6 corrected fare must win dedup).
Both over-link the nightly dispatch path on F2 (Batch Connector Jobs, DAG Scheduler) where the copy job and DAG already exist; judged borderline, not counted, but it inflates F2 for both.
Neither set missed a required component; the gap between them is entirely over-linking, mostly Y's.
